slides.title: Ropedia raises $22M to scale human-centric data collection for embodied AI
slides.tldr: ROPEDIA RAISES $22M FOR EMBODIED AI DATA COLLECTION
slides.highlight: Ropedia is scaling human-centric data collection for embodied AI, which is relevant to the development of social robots and human-robot interaction in RwB.

slides.title: Modeling Duelling Contagions of True and False Information in the Face of Inherent Individual biases
slides.tldr: AGENT-BASED MODELING OF INFORMATION DIFFUSION AND COGNITIVE BIAS
slides.highlight: This research proposes an agent-based co-diffusion model to analyze how network dynamics and cognitive biases influence the spread of competing true and false narratives, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: An agent-based model shows how early seeding and cognitive biases drive the spread of competing narratives.
card.key_idea: A co-diffusion model combining complex-contagion and spiral-of-silence theories to analyze how network dynamics and individual biases affect true versus false information spread.

slides.title: When Shippers Become Algorithms: Candidate Exposure, Information Design, and the Concentration of LLM-Mediated Freight Markets
slides.tldr: LLM AGENTS INCREASE MARKET CONCENTRATION IN FREIGHT MATCHING
slides.highlight: This research uses agent-based simulations with LLMs to analyze how information design affects market concentration, providing insights for MIMIC's study of societal-scale simulation and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: LLM-mediated freight markets risk extreme carrier concentration, which can be mitigated by disclosing real-time capacity.
card.key_idea: Agent-based simulations using GPT, Claude, and Gemini shippers show 'algorithmic monoculture' where models converge on the same carrier, though congestion pricing partially offsets this.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 226 experimental cells (190k decisions) across 30-day simulations. Results are compared against random and deterministic baselines using Mann-Whitney and Wilcoxon tests.
card.limitation: Reliability only affects reviews, not physical delivery outcomes; the study omits a direct channel from reliability to service failure.

slides.title: Not Forgotten: Implementation and Evaluation of a Personalized Episodic Memory for the Humanoid Robot Head Kim
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that a personalized episodic memory module for a humanoid robot head increases perceived trustworthiness and warmth. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Episodic memory in a humanoid robot head increases perceived sociability without increasing user disturbance.
card.key_idea: A lightweight module using vector-based semantic retrieval and a hybrid scoring function (combining cosine similarity, recency, access frequency, and emotional intensity) to inject past interactions into LLM prompts.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects video-based study (N=43) using the HRIES scale; results showed significant gains in trustworthiness (d=0.62) and warmth (d=0.56).
card.limitation: Video-based format lacked real-time interaction and ecological validity; results may not generalize beyond the small student sample.

slides.title: Teachy Mini: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Knowledge-Based Generative Social Robot for Higher Education
slides.tldr: KNOWLEDGE-BASED GENERATIVE SOCIAL ROBOT FOR TUTORING
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how knowledge-based design and retrieval-augmented generation can create responsible tutoring behavior in social robots, aligning with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

card.one_liner: Teachy Mini is a knowledge-based generative social robot designed for responsible and personalized higher education tutoring.
card.key_idea: It operationalizes Knowledge-Based Design (KBD) using system prompting, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and stateful prompt orchestration to integrate self-, user-, and context-knowledge.
card.evaluation: A between-subjects study (N=24) compared Teachy Mini to a non-KBD control; results showed significantly higher perceived responsible behavior but no significant differences in acceptance or motivation.
card.limitation: The study was a preliminary evaluation with a small sample size (N=24) using convenience sampling.

slides.title: Reliability-Contagion Feasibility in LLM Multi-Agent Networks
slides.tldr: LLM MULTI-AGENT NETWORK RELIABILITY AND ERROR PROPAGATION
slides.highlight: This research analyzes the trade-off between connectivity and error propagation in LLM multi-agent networks, providing a basis for selecting network topologies under reliability constraints. This is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: Identifies the optimal network connectivity range to balance LLM multi-agent reliability against error propagation risk.
card.key_idea: Couples a correction-aware SEICS epidemic model with a majority-vote reliability benchmark to derive spectral invasion conditions and graph-class feasibility boundaries for heterogeneous communication networks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 21,000 Gillespie simulations and a controlled grok-4.3 experiment on 36 closed-world tasks across three topologies; results align with theoretical predictions.
card.limitation: Reliability benchmark assumes independent signals; real-model experiment uses controlled source reliabilities rather than spontaneous hallucinations.

slides.title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
slides.highlight: StARS uses a recommender system-driven approach to generate user-specific appropriateness scores for robot actions, supporting personalized human-robot interaction aligned with individual norms. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and HRI.

card.one_liner: StARS uses a recommender system approach to personalize socially appropriate robot actions based on individual user preferences.
card.key_idea: A model-agnostic framework integrating collaborative filtering (matrix factorization) with learnable scene representations via residual fusion to predict user-specific appropriateness scores for candidate robot actions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MannersDB+ and SocNav1 using various backbones (MLPs, GNNs). Results show statistically significant improvements in RMSE/MSE, Pearson r, and CCC.

slides.title: ACME: A Multi-Cultural, Multi-Embodiment Social-Navigation Dataset
slides.highlight: This dataset captures goal-driven social navigation and robot-crowd interactions across diverse cultures and embodiments, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: ACME is a large-scale, multi-cultural, multi-embodiment dataset for social robot navigation and pedestrian trajectory prediction.
card.key_idea: Data collected across 5 countries using 7 robot embodiments, featuring onboard multi-modal sensors, robot speech interactions, and human-verified BEV pedestrian trajectories.
card.evaluation: Compared against prior datasets via qualitative/quantitative analysis of scenario complexity and pedestrian behavior; benchmarked SOTA vision navigation and trajectory prediction models.
card.limitation: Varying levels of data anonymization (face blurring to full body segmentation) may hinder the use of off-the-shelf vision models.

slides.title: Italian Startup Debuts Gene.01 Humanoid With Skin That Senses Humans Before Contact
slides.highlight: The Gene.01 humanoid features skin capable of sensing humans before contact, offering potential advancements for human-robot interaction in the context of RwB.

slides.title: STEER: Steerable Dyadic Head Avatars
slides.tldr: CONTROLLABLE DYADIC MOTION PRIOR FOR CONVERSATIONAL AVATARS
slides.highlight: STEER provides explicit control over gaze, head rhythm, and emotion in dyadic head avatars, supporting HyECHO's focus on engagement and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: STEER is a controllable 3D dyadic motion prior for photorealistic, reactive conversational head avatars.
card.key_idea: A causal flow-matching transformer generates target motion conditioned on audio, partner cues, and explicit controls for gaze, head-rhythm, and emotion.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a filtered RealTalk corpus against DualTalk and UniLS; STEER outperformed baselines in motion quality, dynamics, and diversity.
card.limitation: Behavioral labels are derived from kinematic proxies via an annotation pipeline rather than ground-truth social-intent labels.

slides.title: A Case Study on the Acceptance of a Humanoid Robotic Head Employed in Three Public Spaces
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOT ACCEPTANCE IN PUBLIC SPACES
slides.highlight: This study examines user acceptance and interaction with a humanoid robotic head using multimodal, emotion-based verbal responses, contributing to HyECHO's focus on social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: A humanoid robotic head was tested for user acceptance across three different public environments.
card.key_idea: A robot using an emotion simulation backend to generate multimodal, multi-lingual verbal responses based on natural language processing.
card.evaluation: TAM2 questionnaires across three locations; results show general motivation and usability, though acceptance varied by setting.
card.limitation: Slow response times for approximately 20% of users, which impeded the natural flow of dialogue.

slides.title: Moral Hazard in Multi-Agent Language Models
slides.tldr: ANALYZING COOPERATION FAILURE IN MULTI-AGENT LLMS
slides.highlight: This work introduces the Dialogue Moral Hazard Game to study how language agents balance local rewards against costly, socially valuable efforts, providing insights for MIMIC's simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Language models often fail to take costly, other-benefiting actions, even when optimized for team success.
card.key_idea: The Dialogue Moral Hazard Game tests if agents pay a query cost to reveal hidden safety facts that benefit other agents' decisions.
card.evaluation: Seven open-weight models were tested across base, SFT, RLOO, and GEPA conditions using decomposed metrics like query rate and information transfer.
card.limitation: The fixed query-warning-decision pipeline may not capture the complexity of unrestricted negotiation or diverse tool-access scenarios in deployed systems.

slides.title: Low-Latency Turn-Taking via Context-Aware Preface Generation in a Real-World Dialogue Robot
slides.tldr: CONTEXT-AWARE PREFACE GENERATION FOR LOW-LATENCY ROBOT DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: This work proposes a two-stage incremental framework using an intent readiness detector and voice activity projection to reduce response latency. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on engagement and listener modeling within human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: A two-stage framework reduces robot response latency using context-aware prefaces triggered by intent readiness detection.
card.key_idea: Decouples prefatory-response preparation from speech onset using an intent readiness detector (ModernBERT) and a Voice Activity Projection (VAP) model to determine delivery timing.
card.evaluation: Field experiment with a route-guidance robot in a mall; compared no-filler, fixed-filler, and contextual-preface using latency metrics and 7-point Likert scales.
card.limitation: Prefatory and main responses are generated independently, risking semantic/prosodic discontinuity and occasional dialogue breakdowns like fragments or generic questions.

slides.title: WCM: World-Cognition Model for Generalizable Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: HUMAN-CENTERED EMBODIED AGENT FOR INTERACTIVE TEACHING
slides.highlight: The World-Cognition Model (WCM) introduces a human-in-the-loop teaching mode and a concurrent runtime for reasoning and dialogue, supporting the RwB goal of AI-mediated embodied learning.

card.one_liner: WCM is a human-centered robot agent enabling real-time interaction, correction, and learning via a modular architecture.
card.key_idea: Uses the SLAK architecture (Sensing, Logic, Action, Knowledge) and an asynchronous runtime to decouple reasoning from execution, distilling autonomous and human-taught episodes into CoT supervision.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a low-cost mobile platform across nine real-world HRI tasks, achieving a 73.8% average success rate including held-out tasks.
card.limitation: Currently limited by hardware constraints and a case-study based evaluation approach.
